text:
Alex: Heads-up, I want to propose a small follow-up to the offload RFC: switch from passive evict-only host pages to refcounted host pages with periodic liveness scan.
Maria: Hmm, can you sketch the benefits? sounds like more CPU work.
Alex: It's about fragmentation and dangling tails when we move slices around. With refcounts we can compact reclaim more safely and avoid long-lived tiny allocations.
Sam: How does this interact with async offload? we don't want stalls on the render path.
Alex: Plan: maintain a 16-bit refcount in the host page header (atomic), increment on KV-cache pin, decrement on release. Background scanner walks free lists and merges contiguous zero-ref pages.
Lee: What about races: a page could be refcount 0 but still have an in-flight GPU write that hasn't flushed.
Alex: We use a 'quiesce' epoch + write-fence. Sequence: GPU submit -> fence -> increment refcount on pin -> when fence signals, decrement. Scanner only reclaims pages that are zero AND epoch < current-allowed.
Priya: Any perf numbers? increment/decrement atomics on hot path could add latency.
Alex: We measured on a microbenchmark: refcount atomics add ~40ns on hot path, but reduces long tail fragmentation which saves 15% memory and a 7% throughput gain on large prompts.
Maria: Can you paste the pseudo header and scanner loop? makes it easier to review.
Alex: Sure:
```
struct HostPageHdr {
  uint16_t refcount; // atomic
  uint16_t flags;
  uint32_t epoch;
};

// scanner pseudocode
for page in pages:
  if page.refcount==0 && page.epoch < reclaim_epoch:
    try_coalesce(page)
```
Sam: Looks reasonable. But we should avoid walking whole heap every sweep. Suggest hierarchical lists by size-class and a dirty queue from frees.
Alex: Agreed. We'll push frees into a per-NUMA dirty queue; scanner drains those first and only fallbacks to full scan during low-load windows.
Lee: Need to update allocator API: pin_page/unpin_page pair, and a fast-path for stack-allocated temp pins that batch atomics.
Priya: Also add metrics: refcount-inc/dec rate, coalesces/sweep-time, reclaimable-bytes.
Infra-bot: Note: created RFC follow-up issue #482 in repo infra/allocator with Alex as owner.
Maria: Ok, next steps: Alex to draft short RFC update with perf numbers, Sam and Lee to review allocator API changes, Priya to add metrics proposal.
Alex: I'll drop the draft today and ping in here. Thanks :sparkles: :thumbsup:
